tabs.text: Catering is billed separately from venue hire and is charged per person per day for the expected attendance. Among venues that meet all of the event lead's requirements, please book the one with the lowest combined cost of venue hire, AV and catering for both days.

questions.stem: Which of the venues meet all of the event lead's requirements?
choices: The Foundry and Meridian Centre only
Harbourview, The Foundry and Meridian Centre only
questions.explanation: Required capacity is 1.10 × 180 = 198, which rules out Linden Hall (190); Linden Hall is also 35 minutes from the airport. Two-day venue cost: Harbourview 2 × 7,200 = $14,400; The Foundry 2 × (6,500 + 1,200) = $15,400; Meridian Centre 2 × 8,400 = $16,800, over the $16,000 limit. So only Harbourview and The Foundry qualify.

questions.stem: What is the combined two-day cost of venue hire, AV and catering at the venue Finance would book?
questions.explanation: Catering covers 180 + 140 = 320 person-days. Harbourview: 14,400 + 320 × 48 = 14,400 + 15,360 = $29,760. The Foundry: 15,400 + 320 × 42 = 15,400 + 13,440 = $28,840. The Foundry is cheaper, so the answer is $28,840. Leaving out The Foundry's AV fee gives $26,440.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: If expected day-one attendance rose to 190, The Foundry would no longer meet the capacity requirement.
Linden Hall fails only the airport-distance requirement.
Meridian Centre's two-day venue hire exceeds the venue budget by more than $1,000.

questions.explanation: With 190 attendees the required capacity is 209, above The Foundry's 200: Yes. Linden Hall also fails the capacity rule (190 < 198): No. Meridian's two days cost $16,800, which is $800 over budget, not more than $1,000: No.

tabs.title: Protocol summary
tabs.text: Study KT-204 compares an investigational drug, Delvorin, with placebo in adults with moderate plaque psoriasis. Patients are randomly assigned in a 2 : 1 ratio to Delvorin or placebo. The primary endpoint is the proportion of patients reaching PASI-75, a 75 percent improvement in skin-severity score, at week 16. Patients who stop treatment before week 16 are counted as non-responders. A site must pause enrolment if more than 5 percent of its enrolled patients have had a serious adverse event (SAE).

tabs.title: Monitor's e-mail
tabs.text: Two points from my visit. First, at Site B, 2 of the 4 patients with an SAE were on placebo. Second, Site C enrolled 6 patients (4 on Delvorin, 2 on placebo) who did not meet the inclusion criterion for affected body surface area. The sponsor has decided to exclude these 6 patients from the efficacy analysis. None of the 6 reached PASI-75 and none discontinued.

questions.stem: Before any exclusions, what was the PASI-75 response rate among all patients enrolled on Delvorin across the three sites?
questions.explanation: Responders on Delvorin: 26 + 22 + 15 = 63. Enrolled on Delvorin: 40 + 36 + 24 = 100. Because discontinued patients count as non-responders, the denominator is everyone enrolled, so the rate is 63 ÷ 100 = 63 percent. The 66 percent option is the rate after the Site C exclusion (63 ÷ 96), which this question does not ask for.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: Site B must pause enrolment under the protocol.
Site A must pause enrolment under the protocol.
After the exclusion described by the monitor, Site C's Delvorin response rate is above 70 percent.

questions.explanation: Site B has 4 patients with an SAE among 36 + 18 = 54 enrolled, about 7.4 percent, above 5 percent; the arm in which the SAEs occurred does not matter under the rule: Yes. Site A has 2 of 60, about 3.3 percent: No. After removing 4 non-responding Delvorin patients, Site C has 15 responders out of 20, or 75 percent: Yes.

questions.stem: After the 6 Site C patients are excluded, the Delvorin response rate across all three sites exceeds the placebo response rate by approximately how many percentage points?
questions.explanation: Delvorin: 63 responders out of 100 - 4 = 96, about 65.6 percent. Placebo: 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 responders out of 20 + 18 + 12 - 2 = 48, which is 18.75 percent. The difference is about 65.6 - 18.75 = 46.9, or approximately 47 points. Without the exclusion the gap would be 63 - 18 = 45 points.

tabs.title: COO memo
tabs.text: We are evaluating whether to move regional distribution from our current Riverton warehouse to Eastgate or Millbrook, or to stay. The decision criterion is five-year total cost: the one-time relocation cost plus five years of annual operating cost (rent plus transport). We will not choose any site whose average outbound delivery time is more than 2.0 days.

tabs.title: Logistics e-mail
tabs.text: Two updates. First, the transport figures assume current fuel prices; if fuel prices rise 20 percent, annual transport cost at every site rises 8 percent. Second, Millbrook's landlord will cut annual rent by $60 thousand if we sign a ten-year lease, and adding a second carrier at Millbrook would bring its average delivery time down to 1.9 days but raise its annual transport cost by $90 thousand.

questions.stem: Based on the COO's criterion and the table, the chosen option's five-year total cost is lower than that of staying at Riverton by how much?
questions.explanation: Five-year totals: Riverton 5 × (820 + 1,140) = 9,800; Eastgate 950 + 5 × (610 + 1,050) = 950 + 8,300 = 9,250; Millbrook 600 + 5 × 1,800 = 9,600, but Millbrook is excluded by its 2.1-day delivery time. Eastgate is chosen and saves 9,800 - 9,250 = $550 thousand. $1,500 thousand ignores the relocation cost; $200 thousand compares Millbrook with Riverton.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: If fuel prices rose 20 percent, Eastgate's five-year total cost would still be lower than Riverton's.
If Millbrook added the second carrier and signed the ten-year lease, its five-year total cost would be lower than Eastgate's.
If Millbrook added the second carrier but did not sign the ten-year lease, its five-year total cost would exceed Riverton's.

questions.explanation: With 8 percent higher transport, Eastgate is 950 + 5 × (610 + 1,134) = 9,670 and Riverton is 5 × (820 + 1,231.2) = 10,256: Yes. Millbrook with both changes: 600 + 5 × (480 + 1,350) = 600 + 9,150 = 9,750, above Eastgate's 9,250: No. With the carrier only: 600 + 5 × (540 + 1,350) = 10,050, above Riverton's 9,800: Yes.

questions.stem: At current fuel prices, approximately how many years of Eastgate's annual operating savings over Riverton would it take to equal Eastgate's one-time relocation cost?
questions.explanation: Annual operating cost is 820 + 1,140 = 1,960 at Riverton and 610 + 1,050 = 1,660 at Eastgate, so Eastgate saves $300 thousand per year. The relocation cost of $950 thousand is recovered after 950 ÷ 300, about 3.2 years. Using only the rent difference (210) would give about 4.5 years, which is not offered.

tabs.title: Growth lead's e-mail
tabs.text: In March we ran a four-week acquisition test across four paid channels. A customer counts as acquired if he or she makes a first purchase within 14 days of clicking one of our ads. The metric we care about is cost per acquired customer (CPA), which is channel spend divided by acquired customers. For next quarter, any channel whose CPA is more than 25 percent above the blended CPA (total spend divided by total acquired customers) will be cut.

tabs.title: Analytics memo
tabs.text: The acquired-customer figure for Affiliates comes from the partners' own reports, which use a 30-day window rather than our 14-day window. Our audit found that 25 percent of the acquisitions the partners reported happened between day 15 and day 30 after the click. All other channels' figures use our 14-day window.

questions.stem: Based on the e-mail and the table only, which channel or channels will be cut?
questions.explanation: Blended CPA is 120,000 ÷ 2,000 = $60, so the cut-off is 1.25 × 60 = $75. Channel CPAs: Search 45,000 ÷ 900 = $50; Social 30,000 ÷ 500 = $60; Affiliates 25,000 ÷ 400 = $62.50; Video 20,000 ÷ 200 = $100. Only Video is above $75.

questions.stem: If the Affiliates figure is corrected to our 14-day window as described in the memo, what is the Affiliates CPA, to the nearest dollar?
questions.explanation: Removing the 25 percent of acquisitions that fall outside 14 days leaves 0.75 × 400 = 300 Affiliates customers. CPA = 25,000 ÷ 300, about $83.33, or $83. The $78 option is close to the new cut-off rather than the CPA.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: After the correction in the memo, Affiliates would also be cut.
Search had the lowest cost per click of the four channels.
Before the correction, total first-order revenue from Search customers exceeded Search spend.

questions.explanation: After the correction, total acquisitions are 1,900, so blended CPA is 120,000 ÷ 1,900, about $63.16, and the cut-off is about $78.95. Affiliates at about $83.33 is above it: Yes. Cost per click: Search $1.50, Social $0.75, Affiliates $3.13, Video $0.80, so Social is lowest: No. Search revenue is 900 × 62 = $55,800, above $45,000: Yes.

tabs.title: Vendor price sheet
tabs.text:
Basic plan: $18 per user per month; up to 50 GB of storage per user; no single sign-on (SSO).
Pro plan: $27 per user per month; unlimited storage; includes SSO; no audit logs.
Enterprise plan: a flat $9,000 per month covering up to 400 users, plus $15 per user per month for each user above 400; unlimited storage; includes SSO and audit logs.
Paying a full year in advance reduces the price of any plan by 10 percent. All of a customer's users must be on the same plan.

tabs.title: IT director's e-mail
tabs.text: Security policy requires SSO for every user. Compliance requires audit logs only for Finance and Legal users, but because all users must be on one plan, the plan we choose must include audit logs. We will pay annually in advance.

questions.stem: What will the company pay for one year of service on the plan that meets IT's requirements, paying in advance?
questions.explanation: Only Enterprise includes both SSO and audit logs. With 420 users the monthly price is 9,000 + 20 × 15 = $9,300. A year costs 12 × 9,300 = $111,600, and the 10 percent prepayment discount brings it to $100,440. $97,200 ignores the 20 users above 400; $111,600 forgets the discount; $122,472 is the Pro plan with the discount.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: If the audit-log requirement were dropped, the Pro plan paid in advance would cost less per year than the Enterprise plan paid in advance.
Ignoring the SSO and audit-log requirements, the Basic plan's storage limit would meet every department's average storage need.
If the company grew to 500 users, the Enterprise plan's monthly price before any discount would be $10,500.

questions.explanation: Pro for 420 users paid in advance is 420 × 27 × 12 × 0.9 = $122,472, more than Enterprise's $100,440: No. Engineering (85 GB) and Legal (60 GB) average above the 50 GB Basic limit: No. At 500 users Enterprise costs 9,000 + 100 × 15 = $10,500 per month: Yes.

questions.stem: Before discounts, what is the smallest number of users at which the Pro plan's monthly price is greater than the Enterprise plan's monthly price?
questions.explanation: Up to 400 users, Enterprise costs a flat $9,000, so Pro is more expensive once 27n > 9,000, that is, n > 333.3. The smallest whole number is 334 (27 × 334 = $9,018). Above 400 users Pro adds $27 per user against Enterprise's $15, so Pro stays more expensive. 333 users cost $8,991 on Pro, still below $9,000.

tabs.title: Fleet policy
tabs.text: A delivery van is replaced as soon as either (a) its odometer reaches 200,000 km or (b) its maintenance cost over the past 12 months is more than 35 percent of the price of a new diesel van. A new diesel van costs $42,000 and a new electric van costs $55,000. Electric vans qualify for a government rebate of 15 percent of their purchase price, which is received at the time of purchase.

tabs.title: Fleet manager's e-mail
tabs.text: For replacement decisions, use these running costs. Energy: $0.14 per km for diesel and $0.05 per km for electric. Maintenance: $0.06 per km for diesel and $0.03 per km for electric. We keep each new van for five years. When comparing options, total cost means net purchase price (after any rebate) plus energy and maintenance over the van's life.

questions.stem: Which vans meet the replacement policy right now?
questions.explanation: The maintenance threshold is 0.35 × 42,000 = $14,700. V-101 ($16,100) and V-105 ($15,000) exceed it; V-103 ($14,200) and V-104 ($12,500) do not. On the odometer test only V-102 (204,500 km) has reached 200,000; V-104 is at 199,000, just short. So V-101, V-102 and V-105 qualify.

questions.stem: For a replacement van driven 25,000 km per year and kept five years, how much lower is the total cost of an electric van than that of a diesel van?
questions.explanation: Five years at 25,000 km is 125,000 km. Diesel: 42,000 + 125,000 × (0.14 + 0.06) = 42,000 + 25,000 = $67,000. Electric: net price 0.85 × 55,000 = $46,750, plus 125,000 × (0.05 + 0.03) = $10,000, for $56,750. The difference is $10,250. $15,000 counts only running-cost savings (125,000 × 0.12) and ignores the higher net price.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: If V-104 is driven at its typical annual rate, it will reach the odometer threshold within the next month.
An electric van's total cost falls below a diesel van's total cost before the van has been driven 40,000 km.
If the maintenance threshold were raised to 40 percent of a new diesel van's price, V-101 would still meet the replacement policy.

questions.explanation: V-104 drives about 45,000 ÷ 12 = 3,750 km a month, taking it from 199,000 to about 202,750 km: Yes. The electric van costs 46,750 - 42,000 = $4,750 more up front and saves $0.12 per km, so it breaks even after 4,750 ÷ 0.12, about 39,583 km: Yes. A 40 percent threshold is $16,800; V-101's $16,100 is below it and its odometer is under 200,000: No.

tabs.title: Supplier terms
tabs.text: Price per tonne of recycled PET flake depends on the total tonnes a customer orders in a calendar quarter: fewer than 200 tonnes, $820 per tonne; 200 to 399 tonnes, $780 per tonne; 400 tonnes or more, $750 per tonne. The tier price applies to every tonne in that quarter's order, not only to the tonnes above a threshold. Freight is $35 per tonne at every volume. Orders are in whole tonnes and are delivered in the quarter they are placed.

tabs.title: Procurement memo
tabs.text: North and South currently order separately, so each plant's order is priced on its own volume. If the plants order jointly, their quantities are combined for tier purposes. Flake bought early can be stored at the South plant for $12 per tonne for each quarter it is held.

questions.stem: If the plants order jointly each quarter for exactly that quarter's needs, what is the total annual cost of flake including freight?
questions.explanation: Joint quarterly volumes are 210, 250, 250 and 210 tonnes, all in the 200-399 tier, so every tonne costs 780 + 35 = $815. Total volume is 920 tonnes, and 920 × 815 = $749,800. $717,600 leaves out freight, and $786,600 is the cost of ordering separately (every plant order is under 200 tonnes, so 920 × 855).

questions.stem: Suppose the plants order jointly and, in Q2, buy enough flake to cover both Q2 and Q3 needs, storing the Q3 portion for one quarter. Compared with ordering jointly in each of Q2 and Q3, how much lower is the combined cost of flake, freight and storage for those two quarters?
questions.explanation: Q2 plus Q3 need is 250 + 250 = 500 tonnes, which reaches the $750 tier. Flake savings: 500 × (780 - 750) = $15,000. Freight is the same per tonne either way. Storing the Q3 portion costs 250 × 12 = $3,000. Net saving: 15,000 - 3,000 = $12,000. Choosing $15,000 ignores storage.

tabs.title: Protocol
tabs.text: This phase II study tests three doses of Ambrexil (25 mg, 50 mg and 100 mg) against placebo for preventing migraine. The primary endpoint is the reduction in mean monthly migraine days from baseline to week 12. A dose may be taken into phase III only if (1) its mean reduction exceeds the placebo arm's mean reduction by at least 1.5 days and (2) no more than 8 percent of its patients discontinued because of a treatment-related adverse event (AE).

cols: Mean migraine days per month, baseline
Mean migraine days per month, week 12

tabs.title: Medical lead's e-mail
tabs.text: The safety committee has reviewed the 50 mg arm and reclassified two discontinuations, previously recorded as unrelated to treatment, as treatment-related. Separately, our licensing partner has said it would accept, for phase III, a dose whose treatment-related AE discontinuation rate is as high as 10 percent, provided its mean reduction exceeds placebo's by at least 2.5 days.

questions.stem: Based on the protocol and the table only, which doses may be taken into phase III?
questions.explanation: Mean reductions: placebo 9.4 - 8.1 = 1.3; 25 mg 2.0; 50 mg 3.1; 100 mg 3.9. Advantages over placebo: 0.7, 1.8 and 2.6 days, so 25 mg fails the efficacy test. AE discontinuation rates: 50 mg 5 ÷ 78, about 6.4 percent, passes; 100 mg 9 ÷ 82, about 11.0 percent, fails. Only 50 mg qualifies.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: After the reclassification in the e-mail, the 50 mg dose still meets the protocol's AE criterion.
The 100 mg dose would meet the licensing partner's alternative standard.
The 100 mg arm's mean reduction exceeds placebo's by more than 2.5 days.

questions.explanation: With two more treatment-related discontinuations, 50 mg has 7 of 78, about 9.0 percent, above 8 percent: No. The 100 mg dose has the required 2.6-day advantage, but its AE rate of about 11.0 percent exceeds the partner's 10 percent ceiling: No. Its advantage is 3.9 - 1.3 = 2.6 days, more than 2.5: Yes.

questions.stem: What is the greatest number of treatment-related AE discontinuations the 100 mg arm could have had and still met the licensing partner's alternative standard?
questions.explanation: The partner allows a rate of at most 10 percent. With 82 patients, 10 percent is 8.2, so at most 8 discontinuations (8 ÷ 82, about 9.8 percent) are allowed; 9 gives about 11.0 percent. The efficacy condition (2.6 days ≥ 2.5) is already met, so the answer is 8.

tabs.title: Strategy memo
tabs.text: We will open at most two new stores next year. A candidate location qualifies only if its payback period, defined as fit-out cost divided by projected annual operating profit, is under 3 years. Projected annual operating profit is projected annual revenue times the operating margin. Among qualifying locations we will choose the two with the highest combined projected annual operating profit, except that the two new stores may not be in the same metro area.

tabs.title: CFO e-mail
tabs.text: One constraint the memo leaves out: our capital budget for store fit-outs next year is $2.6 million in total, so the combined fit-out cost of the two new stores cannot exceed that. Separately, our negotiations with the Dune Road landlord may reduce Dune Road's fit-out cost by $100 thousand.

questions.stem: Based on the strategy memo and the table only, which two locations would be chosen?
questions.explanation: Annual profits ($ thousands): Alder 432, Bay 528, Cedar 312, Dune 360, Elm 490. Paybacks: Alder 2.78, Bay 2.84, Cedar 2.88, Dune 3.06 (fails), Elm 2.65. The two highest qualifying profits are Bay (528) and Elm (490), in different metros, so Bay Street and Elm Square. Alder and Bay are both in Northvale, so that pair is not allowed.

questions.stem: Once the CFO's capital budget is taken into account, what is the combined projected annual operating profit of the pair chosen?
questions.explanation: Bay and Elm need 1,500 + 1,300 = 2,800, over the 2,600 budget. Check allowed pairs in different metros within budget: Alder + Elm (2,500) gives 432 + 490 = 922; Bay + Cedar (2,400) gives 840; Elm + Cedar (2,200) gives 802; Alder + Cedar gives 744. The best is Alder Park and Elm Square at $922 thousand. $1,018 thousand is Bay plus Elm, which breaks the budget.

If Dune Road's fit-out cost fell by $100 thousand, Dune Road would qualify under the payback rule.
If Dune Road's fit-out cost fell by $100 thousand, the best pair within the CFO's budget would include Dune Road.

tabs.title: Pricing team e-mail
tabs.text: We tested three monthly prices for our meal-planning subscription. For four weeks, visitors to the sign-up page were randomly assigned to see one price, and each price was shown to 12,000 visitors. Monthly contribution per subscriber is the price minus a variable cost of $3.50 (payment fees and support). We will choose the price that maximises expected contribution per visitor over a subscriber's first six months, calculated as (sign-ups ÷ visitors) × average months subscribed in the first six months × monthly contribution.

cols: Average months subscribed in first six months

tabs.title: Finance memo
tabs.text: From next month our payment processor raises its fees, so variable cost will be $4.50 per subscriber per month instead of $3.50. Marketing is also considering a 20 percent discount on the first month only, at whichever price is chosen. Analysts expect the discount to raise sign-ups by 15 percent without changing average months subscribed; the discount reduces first-month revenue only.

questions.stem: Using the pricing team's method and the original $3.50 variable cost, the expected contribution per visitor at $14.99 is closest to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Sign-up rate at $14.99 is 450 ÷ 12,000 = 0.0375. Monthly contribution is 14.99 - 3.50 = $11.49, over an average of 5.0 months, or $57.45 per subscriber. Per visitor: 0.0375 × 57.45, about $2.154, closest to $2.15. For comparison, $9.99 gives 0.06 × 4.5 × 6.49, about $1.75, and $12.99 gives 0.045 × 4.8 × 9.49, about $2.05.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: At the original variable cost, $12.99 yields more expected contribution per visitor than $9.99.
After the variable-cost increase in the memo, the price that maximises expected contribution per visitor changes.
At the higher variable cost, offering the first-month discount at $14.99 would raise expected contribution per visitor at that price.

questions.explanation: At $3.50: $9.99 gives about $1.75 and $12.99 about $2.05: Yes. At $4.50: $9.99 gives 0.06 × 4.5 × 5.49, about $1.48; $12.99 gives 0.045 × 4.8 × 8.49, about $1.83; $14.99 gives 0.0375 × 5 × 10.49, about $1.97, so $14.99 still wins: No. With the discount, sign-ups rise to 517.5 (rate 0.043125) and each subscriber contributes 5 × 10.49 - 0.2 × 14.99, about $49.45, giving about $2.13 per visitor, above $1.97: Yes.

questions.stem: At the original variable cost, by approximately what percent would sign-ups at $9.99 have had to be higher for $9.99 to match the expected contribution per visitor at $14.99?
questions.explanation: Contribution per visitor is proportional to sign-ups when price and retention are fixed. $14.99 yields about $2.154 and $9.99 about $1.752 per visitor. The ratio 2.154 ÷ 1.752 is about 1.23, so sign-ups at $9.99 would need to be about 23 percent higher, roughly 885 instead of 720. A quick estimate: 57.45 ÷ 29.2 (contribution per subscriber) is about 1.97, and 450 × 1.97 ≈ 885.

tabs.title: Fund rules
tabs.text: The Halden Foundation's innovation fund has $1.2 million to award this year. Each proposal receives either its full requested amount or nothing. Any set of awards must satisfy three rules: (1) the total awarded may not exceed the fund; (2) at least 40 percent of the total awarded must go to proposals led by small organisations; (3) no single region may receive more than half of the total awarded. Among all sets of awards that satisfy the rules, the committee chooses the one that awards the largest total amount; if two or more sets tie on total amount, it chooses the one with the highest combined review score.

tabs.title: Programme officer's e-mail
tabs.text: Late update: the applicant behind P4 has revised its budget and reduced its request from $400 thousand to $300 thousand. Nothing else about P4 has changed. Please rerun the allocation with the revised figure.

questions.stem: Using the original requests, which proposals will be funded?
questions.explanation: Four proposals always break a rule: any four requests total at least $1,100 thousand, and the only four-proposal sets within $1.2 million either give small organisations under 40 percent or give one region more than half. The largest valid totals are $950 thousand, reached by P2, P3, P4 (small share 550 of 950; regions 300, 250, 400, none above 475) and by P1, P2, P6 (small 500 of 950; North 450, South 300, East 200). Both total $950 thousand, so the tie goes to the higher score: 88 + 85 + 83 = 256 beats 92 + 88 + 74 = 254. P1, P2, P3 and P6 totals 1,200 but North gets 700, more than half.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: No set of awards that satisfies the rules funds both P1 and P4.
Under the original requests, more than half of the total awarded goes to small organisations.
If the fund were only $900 thousand, the same proposals would be funded.

questions.explanation: P1 and P4 together are $850 thousand from large organisations. If small awards total s, rule 2 needs s ≥ 0.4(850 + s), so s ≥ about 567, but then the total would exceed $1.2 million: Yes. Small organisations receive 300 + 250 = 550 of 950, about 58 percent: Yes. The chosen set totals $950 thousand, which a $900 thousand fund could not cover: No.

questions.stem: After P4's request is reduced as described in the e-mail, which proposal that was funded under the original requests would no longer be funded?
choices: None of them; P2, P3 and P4 are all still funded
questions.explanation: With P4 at $300 thousand, the set P3, P4, P5, P6 totals 250 + 300 + 350 + 200 = $1,100 thousand. Small share: 450 of 1,100, about 41 percent. Regions: North 250, East 500, South 350, none above 550. No valid set awards more (P2, P3, P4, P6 totals only 1,050). So the new allocation is P3, P4, P5 and P6, and P2, despite its high score, drops out, because the rule favours the largest total awarded before the review score.

tabs.title: Nurse manager's memo
tabs.text: Ward 6 requires the following minimum number of registered nurses on duty at every moment of each day: 06:00-14:00, at least 6; 14:00-22:00, at least 5; 22:00-06:00, at least 3. Nurses work one of five shift types. Eight-hour shifts start at 06:00, 14:00 or 22:00. Twelve-hour shifts run 06:00-18:00 (day) or 18:00-06:00 (night). We want the lowest-cost daily schedule that meets these minimums.

tabs.title: HR e-mail
tabs.text: Please note the union agreement that takes effect next month. Each day, at least half of all shifts scheduled must be 8-hour shifts, and no more than 4 shifts in total may be 12-hour shifts.

questions.stem: Using only 8-hour shifts, what is the lowest possible daily cost of meeting the minimums?
questions.explanation: With only 8-hour shifts, each block is covered by its own shift type, so the cheapest schedule uses exactly the minimum in each: 6 day shifts, 5 evening shifts and 3 night shifts. Cost: 6 × 400 + 5 × 440 + 3 × 480 = 2,400 + 2,200 + 1,440 = $6,040.

questions.stem: Ignoring the union agreement, what is the lowest possible daily cost of meeting the minimums?
questions.explanation: A 12-hour day shift covers 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-18:00, and a 12-hour night shift covers 18:00-22:00 and 22:00-06:00. One of each ($1,240) replaces one 8-hour day, evening and night shift ($1,320), saving $80 per pair. Pairs can replace up to 3 night shifts, giving 3 day, 2 evening, 0 night, 3 twelve-hour day and 3 twelve-hour night shifts: 1,200 + 880 + 1,680 + 2,040 = $5,800. Checking all combinations confirms nothing cheaper meets every block.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: Under the union agreement, the lowest possible daily cost is $5,880.
The lowest-cost schedule when the union agreement is ignored breaks the agreement's limit on 12-hour shifts.
Under the union agreement, the lowest-cost schedule includes no 8-hour night shift.

questions.explanation: The agreement allows at most 4 twelve-hour shifts, so at most 2 of the $80-saving pairs: 4 day, 3 evening, 1 night, 2 twelve-hour day and 2 twelve-hour night shifts cost 1,600 + 1,320 + 480 + 1,120 + 1,360 = $5,880, and 8 of the 12 shifts are 8-hour shifts: Yes. The unrestricted optimum uses 6 twelve-hour shifts, more than 4: Yes. The union-compliant optimum has 2 twelve-hour night shifts covering 22:00-06:00, so it still needs 1 eight-hour night shift to reach 3 nurses: No.

tabs.title: Integration memo
tabs.text: After acquiring Brightline, we will review the two companies' offices in each of three cities. In each city we either keep both offices or close one and move all of its staff into the other. Because of hybrid working, a receiving office must have at least 0.8 desks per person for the combined staff of both offices. Closing an office saves its annual lease, but in the first year it also incurs a one-time exit fee equal to 50 percent of that office's annual lease, plus moving costs of $2,500 per person moved. First-year net savings equal lease savings minus exit fees and moving costs.

tabs.title: CFO e-mail
tabs.text: Good news on Denver: the Brightline Denver lease has a break clause, so if we close that office we will pay no exit fee there. All other exit fees stand. The board wants first-year net savings of at least $1.5 million, achieved with as few office closures as possible.

questions.stem: Under the desk rule in the memo, which offices could be closed?
choices: Only the Brightline office in Denver
Only our offices in Austin and Raleigh
The Brightline offices in Austin and Raleigh only
Our offices in all three cities
The Brightline offices in all three cities
questions.explanation: Required desks are 0.8 × combined staff. Denver: 0.8 × 360 = 288; our office has 300 desks, Brightline 160, so only Brightline can close. Austin: 0.8 × 200 = 160; ours has 170, Brightline 140, so only Brightline can close. Raleigh: 0.8 × 110 = 88; ours has 90, Brightline 40, so only Brightline can close. Hence the Brightline office in each of the three cities can be closed, and none of ours can.

questions.prompt: For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true based on the information provided. Otherwise select No.

statements.text: Before the CFO's update, closing all three Brightline offices would give first-year net savings of less than $1 million.
With the Denver exit fee waived, closing all three Brightline offices would give first-year net savings above $1.7 million.
Moving the staff of our Raleigh office into the Brightline Raleigh office would satisfy the desk rule.

questions.explanation: First-year net savings (in USD thousands): Denver 1,600 - 800 - 140 × 2.5 = 450; Austin 1,300 - 650 - 275 = 375; Raleigh 500 - 250 - 125 = 125; total 950, under 1,000: Yes. Waiving Denver's $800 thousand fee raises the total to 1,750: Yes. The Brightline Raleigh office has 40 desks, far below the 88 needed: No.

questions.stem: Taking the CFO's update into account, which closures meet the board's target with as few closures as possible?
questions.explanation: With no exit fee, closing Brightline Denver saves 1,600 - 350 = $1,250 thousand, short of 1,500, so one closure is not enough. Two-closure options: Denver + Austin = 1,250 + 375 = 1,625, which meets the target; Denver + Raleigh = 1,375, which does not; Austin + Raleigh = 500, which does not. So the board should close Brightline Denver and Brightline Austin. Closing all three also works but uses an extra closure.
